reason: The text explicitly demonstrates collaboration between Nehemiah (the leader) and the people of Jerusalem. Nehemiah addresses the people saying 'Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem' (לְכ֗וּ וְנִבְנֶה֙ אֶת־ חוֹמַ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם). The people respond with unified commitment: 'Let us rise up and build, and they strengthened their hands for the good' (וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ נָק֣וּם וּבָנִ֔ינוּ וַיְחַזְּק֥וּ יְדֵיהֶ֖ם לַטּוֹבָֽה). When facing opposition, Nehemiah speaks on behalf of the united group: 'we His servants will rise and build' (וַאֲנַ֥חְנוּ עֲבָדָ֖יו נָק֣וּם וּבָנִ֑ינוּ), demonstrating coordinated action between leader and people toward a common goal of rebuilding Jerusalem's walls.
